policy: A tool under tools/ that no script, no workflow and no import reaches is a question nobody asks. Each entry here says what the file is instead of a step, and the entries ratchet both ways: a declared file something starts calling fails, and a declaration for a file that is gone fails.

tools.reason: A report a person runs when that question comes up. It reads the tree and prints findings, and fails nothing, so a stage that ran it would add a reading no build can go red on; the gates it overlaps — dead CSS, route consolidation, stored records — are the ones that fail.

A gate no stage asks. Seven of these eight run clean against this tree today; `check-app-page-style-consistency` is red until its audit document is regenerated. Wiring each one is a decision about which stage owns that question, and until it is made they are declared here so the silence is a line a person wrote rather than a script nobody noticed.

A companion to a gate rather than a gate: it proposes a patch and a person reads it before applying. The gate that holds the baseline runs on every commit; this is the tool a reviewer reaches for when that baseline has to move.

The Visio stencil build has no npm script on purpose: `package.json` is an input to the browser walk's fresh-build gate, so adding one would refuse a build that is still current. It is run by hand when a symbol changes, and the package it writes is deterministic down to the byte.

A builder that reads a source document and rewrites catalogue data from it. The document is not in the tree, so there is no stage that could run this: it is called when a new price list, product guide or canonical export lands, and its output is reviewed before it is kept.
A runner rather than a gate: it starts a server, a spec harness or a load driver for a person checking one thing by hand. Its subject is a running stack, which a verify stage does not own.

A writer that changed stored data once, kept as the record of what that change was. Running it again is not a step in any pipeline: it rewrites records from a snapshot of the tree it was written against, so a stage that ran it would either do nothing or do something nobody asked for.

The measurement behind the order gate's settled half: run by hand with `--write` when a route's markup changes, and re-proved on every browser walk through `lib/route-order-settlement.mjs`. A stage cannot run it because it opens a page.
